first_abnormal_boundary.reason: NGAP DownlinkNASTransport (procedure code 4) at frame 18 delivers a security-protected NAS message inside observation window 17-19. The inner 5GSM payload is ciphered (nas-5gs.security_header_type 2, only nas-5gs.ciphered_msg exposed, no mm or sm message type), so no PDU session establishment reject and no 5GSM cause are decodable from this capture. Within the captured N2 scope no NGAP PDUSessionResourceSetup (procedure code 29) follows, and the capture holds no N4 or N3 traffic, so absence of a PFCP session is not evidence. The unsupported-DNN rejection is therefore derived from the protected NAS exchange plus absent N2 resource allocation; upstream fault-injection intent is not packet evidence.

limitations: NAS traffic after Security Mode is encrypted; exact 5GSM cause is protected in envelope
Frames 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21 expose nas-5gs.security_header_type 2 or 4 with only nas-5gs.ciphered_msg present, so no NAS-5GS message type is decodable at those frames
UplinkNASTransport and DownlinkNASTransport are NGAP (TS 38.413) message identities; the NAS-5GS layer contributes no message identity at those frames
Capture contains no N4 (PFCP) and no N3 (GTP-U) traffic, so absence of a PFCP session cannot support a rejection finding
NGAP procedure code 29 (PDUSessionResourceSetup) never appears in the captured N2 scope
